Class NavalHydrodynamicsFreightEngine

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.core.engine.AbstractSimulationEngine
org.ether.society.engines.tier2.theories.NavalHydrodynamicsFreightEngine
All Implemented Interfaces:
SimulationEngineModule
public class NavalHydrodynamicsFreightEngine extends AbstractSimulationEngine

Naval Hydrodynamics & Maritime Freight Index Engine

Models real maritime bulk shipping transport costs across global sea lanes. Replaces synthetic 5-stage subtraction sigmoids with authentic vessel hydrodynamics, payload displacement scaling, and propulsion fuel economics (Froude 1874; Harley 1988).

Scientific Foundations

  • C. Knick Harley (1988) Ocean Freight Rates and New World Expansion 1750–1913, J. Econ. Hist. 48(4): 851–876.
  • William Froude (1874) On the Comparative Resistances of Long Ships of Several Formations, Royal Institution of Naval Architects.
  • Saif I. Mohammed & Jeffrey G. Williamson (2004) Freight Rates and Productivity Gains in British Tramp Shipping 1869–1950, Explorations in Econ. Hist. 41(2): 172–203.

Hydrodynamic Principles

The real economic freight cost per metric ton-kilometer is inversely proportional to vessel payload displacement $\Delta_{\text{payload}}$ and propulsion thermal efficiency: $$C_{\text{freight}} = C_0 \cdot \frac{\text{Opex}_{\text{crew}} + \text{FuelExpenditure}}{\Delta_{\text{payload}} \cdot v_{\text{effective}}}$$

  • Ancient Oared Galleys & Small Cabotage Cogs: Tiny displacement ($\sim 50\text{--}150\text{ tons}$), high crew requirement ($\sim 50\text{--}150$ rowers/sailors). Freight index $\approx 1400$.
  • Age of Sail Full-Rigged Oceanic Ships (Fluyts, Caravels, Indiamen): Large hold ($\sim 400\text{--}1200\text{ tons}$), small crew ($\sim 15\text{--}30$ men), copper sheathing reducing marine fouling. Freight index drops to $\sim 200\text{--}300$.
  • Steam & Steel Propeller Freighters (1870–1914): Triple-expansion marine steam engines, iron/steel hulls eliminating wood hogging, screw propellers. Freight index drops to $\sim 56$.
  • Modern Post-Panamax Containerization (1960–2026): Automated diesel turbine bulk carriers ($50\,000\text{--}200\,000\text{ DWT}$). Freight index drops to $\sim 20$.
